b.c18487f3b4:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>Æ</c>térne Rex altíssime,
Redémptor et fidélium,
Quo mors solúta déperit,
Datur triúmphum grátiæ.

<h>S</h>candens tribúnal déxteræ
Patris, potéstas ómnium
Colláta Jesu cǽlitus,
Quæ non erat humánitus:

<h>U</h>t trina rerum máchina,
Cæléstium, terréstrium,
Et inferórum cóndita,
Flectat genu jam súbdita.

<h>T</h>remunt vidéntes Angeli
Versam vicem mortálium:
Culpat caro, purgat caro,
Regnat Deus Dei caro.

<h>T</h>u esto nostrum gáudium,
Manens olýmpo prǽditum:
Mundi regis qui fábricam,
Mundána vincens gáudia.

<h>I</h>esu, tibi sit glória,
Qui victor in cælum redis,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
b.ae29f3b7d3:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>E</c>ternal Monarch, King most high,
Whose blood hath brought redemption nigh,
By whom the death of death was wrought,
And conquering grace's battle fought:

<h>A</h>scending by the starry road,
This day thou wentest home to God,
By heaven to power unending called,
And by no human hand installed.

<h>T</h>hat so, in nature's triple frame,
Each heavenly and each earthly name,
And things in hell's abyss abhorred,
May bend the knee and own him Lord.

<h>Y</h>ea, angels tremble when they see
How changed is our humanity;
That flesh hath purged what flesh had stained,
And God, the flesh of God, hath reigned.

<h>B</h>e thou our joy, O mighty Lord,
As thou wilt be our great reward;
Earth's joys to thee are nothing worth,
Thou joy and crown of heaven and earth.

<h>A</h>ll glory, Lord, to thee we pay,
Ascending o'er the stars today;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

De Actibus Apostolórum
<r>Act 3:1-5</r>
<n>1</n> Petrus autem et Joánnes ascendébant in templum ad horam oratiónis nonam.
<n>2</n> Et quidam vir, qui erat claudus ex útero matris suæ, bajulabátur; quem ponébant cotídie ad portam templi, quæ dícitur Speciósa, ut péteret eleemósynam ab introëúntibus in templum.
<n>3</n> Is, cum vidísset Petrum et Joánnem incipiéntes introíre in templum, rogábat ut eleemósynam accíperet.
<n>4</n> Intuens autem in eum Petrus cum Joánne, dixit: Réspice in nos.
<n>5</n> At ille intendébat in eos, sperans se áliquid acceptúrum ab eis.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Act. 1:1-2</r>
<c>P</c>rimum quidem sermónem feci de ómnibus, o Theóphile, quæ cœpit Jesus fácere et docére usque in diem, qua præcípiens Apóstolis per Spíritum Sanctum, quos elégit, assúmptus est.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>T</c>u, Christe, nostrum gáudium,
Manens Olýmpo prǽditum:
Mundi regis qui fábricam,
Mundána vincens gáudia.

<h>H</h>inc te precántes quǽsumus,
Ignósce culpis ómnibus
Et corda sursum súbleva
Ad te supérna grátia.

<h>U</h>t cum repénte cœperis
Clarére nube Júdicis,
Pœnas repéllas débitas,
Reddas corónas pérditas.

<h>T</h>u esto nostrum gáudium,
Qui es futúrus prǽmium:
Sit nostra in te glória,
Per cuncta semper sǽcula.

<h>G</h>lória tibi, Dómine,
Qui scandis supra sídera,
Cum Patre, et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> A summo cœlo egréssio ejus, allelúia.
<r>℟.</r> Et occúrsus ejus usque ad summum ejus, allelúia.
b.644108c367:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Act. 1:1-2</r>
<c>T</c>he former treatise I made, O Theophilus, of all things which Jesus began to do and to teach, Until the day on which, giving commandments by the Holy Ghost to the apostles whom he had chosen, he was taken up.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>u, Christe, nostrum gáudium,
Manens Olýmpo prǽditum:
Mundi regis qui fábricam,
Overcoming the joys of the world.

Therefore we pray and beseech thee,
Forgive all our faults
Et corda sursum súbleva
To thee by heavenly grace.

<h>U</h>t cum repénte cœperis
To shine in the cloud of the Judge,
Mayest thou turn away the punishments we deserve,
And give back the crowns we have lost.

<h>T</h>u esto nostrum gáudium,
Thou who art to be our reward:
Sit nostra in te glória,
Per cuncta semper sǽcula.

Glory be to thee, O Lord,
Qui scandis supra sídera,
Cum Patre, et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> His going out is from the end of heaven, alleluia.
<r>℟.</r> And his circuit even to the end thereof, alleluia.

<h>O</h>ctáva Ascensiónis Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.
<h>S</h>ancti Robérti Bellarmíno, e Societáte Jesu, Cardinális atque olim Epíscopi Capuáni, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, cujus dies natális décimo quinto Kaléndas Octóbris recensétur.
<h>R</h>omæ Dedicátio Ecclésiæ sanctæ Maríæ ad Mártyres, quam beátus Bonifátius Papa Quartus, expurgáto deórum ómnium véteri fano, quod Pántheon vocabátur, in honórem beátæ semper Vírginis Maríæ et ómnium Mártyrum dedicávit, témpore Phocæ Imperatóris. Ipsíus vero Dedicatiónis ánnuam solemnitátem póstmodum Summus Póntifex Gregórius item Quartus ab univérsa Ecclésia, et in honórem quidem ómnium Sanctórum, Kaléndis Novémbris agéndam esse constítuit.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli beáti Múcii, Presbýteri et Mártyris; qui, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre et Laudício Procónsule, prius Amphípoli, in Macedónia, multis pœnis atque cruciátibus ob Christi confessiónem afflíctus, póstea, Byzántium usque perdúctus, capitáli senténtia occúbuit.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, ob fidem cathólicam, ab Ariánis in Ecclésia Theónæ occísi sunt.
<h>H</h>eracléæ, in Thrácia, sanctæ Glycériæ, Mártyris Románæ, quæ, sub Antoníno Imperatóre et Sabíno Prǽside, cum fuísset plúrimis ac diris tentáta supplíciis et ab his divína ope incólumis evasísset, tandem feris est obiécta, earúmque una, morsum córpori ipsíus infigénte, spíritum Deo réddidit.
<h>A</h>pud Traiéctum sancti Servátii, Tungrénsis Ecclésiæ Epíscopi; ad cujus méritum ómnibus demonstrándum, dum témpore híemis ómnia in circúitu nix repléret, sepúlcrum ejus numquam opéruit, donec, ex indústria cívium, Basílica super illud ædificáta est.
<h>I</h>n Palæstína sancti Joánnis Silentiárii, qui, Coloniénsi in Arménia Episcopátu dimísso, in sancti Sabbæ laura monásticam vitam duxit, et sancto fine quiévit.
<h>P</h>ódii, in diœcési Pictaviénsi, sancti Andréæ Hubérti Fournet, Confessóris, olim párochi, Institúti Filiárum a Cruce una cum sancta Elísabeth Bichier des Ages Fundatóris, quem Pius Papa Undécimus Sanctórum fastis adscrípsit.

<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>M</c>ay 13th 2027, the 7th day of the Moon,
<h>T</h>he Octave of the Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ.
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Virgin Walburg, of whom mention is made upon the 1st day of May.
<h>U</h>pon the same 13th day of May is kept at Rome the dedication of the church of St. Mary-of-the-Martyrs; this building was called the Pantheon or temple of All the gods, but the blessed Pope Boniface IV cleansed that old temple, and consecrated it in honour of the blessed Mary, always a Virgin, and of All Martyrs, in the time of the Emperor Phocas.
<h>O</h>n the same day, were born into the better life:

<h>A</h>t Constantinople, the blessed martyr Mucius, the Priest. Under the Emperor Diocletian and the Pro-Consul Laodicius, he was first tormented at Amphipolis with many pains and sufferings, on account of his confession of Christ, and afterwards brought to Byzantium, where he was beheaded.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria are commemorated a great number of holy martyrs who were massacred by the Arians in the church of Theona, on account of the Catholic faith, [in the year 372.]
<h>A</h>t Heraclea, the holy martyr Glyceria of Rome, who suffered under the Emperor Antoninus and the President Sabinus.
<h>A</h>t Utrecht, holy Servatius, Bishop of the Church of Tongres. His worthiness was strikingly set forth to all by this, that when everything round about was covered with snow in the winter time, his grave was never covered therewith until a Cathedral Church was built over it by the industry of the citizens.
<h>I</h>n Palestine, [in the year 558,] holy John, surnamed the Silent.

<c>E</c>ternal Monarch, King most high,
Whose blood hath brought redemption nigh,
By whom the death of death was wrought,
And conquering grace's battle fought:

<h>A</h>scending by the starry road,
This day thou wentest home to God,
By heaven to power unending called,
And by no human hand installed.

<h>T</h>hat so, in nature's triple frame,
Each heavenly and each earthly name,
And things in hell's abyss abhorred,
May bend the knee and own him Lord.

<h>Y</h>ea, angels tremble when they see
How changed is our humanity;
That flesh hath purged what flesh had stained,
And God, the flesh of God, hath reigned.

As thou wilt be our great reward;
Earth's joys to thee are nothing worth,
Thou joy and crown of heaven and earth.

<h>A</h>ll glory, Lord, to thee we pay,
Ascending o'er the stars today;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.

b.dc739fa65c:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>I</c>esu nostra redémptio,
Amor et desidérium,
Deus Creátor ómnium,
Homo in fine témporum:

<h>Q</h>uæ te vicit cleméntia,
Ut ferres nostra crímina,
Crudélem mortem pátiens,
Ut nos a morte tólleres!

<h>I</h>nférni claustra pénetrans,
Tuos captívos rédimens,
Victor triúmpho nóbili
Ad dextram Patris résidens.

<h>I</h>psa te cogat píetas,
Ut mala nostra súperes
Parcéndo, et voti cómpotes
Nos tuo vultu sáties.

<h>T</h>u esto nostrum gáudium,
Qui es futúrus prǽmium,
Sit nostra in te glória,
Per cuncta semper sǽcula.

<h>G</h>lória tibi Dómine,
Qui scandis super sídera,
Cum Patre, et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Custódi nos, Dómine, ut pupíllam óculi, allelúia.
<r>℟.</r> Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege nos, allelúia.
b.81fd451f3d:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>H</c>ail, thou who man's Redeemer art,
Jesu, the joy of every heart;
Great Maker of the world's wide frame,
And purest love's delight and flame:

<h>W</h>hat nameless mercy thee o'ercame,
To bear our load of sin and shame?
For guiltless, thou thy life didst give,
That sinful erring man might live.

<h>T</h>he realms of woe are forced by thee,
Its captives from their chains set free;
And thou, amid thy ransomed train,
At God's right hand dost victor reign.

<h>L</h>et mercy sweet with thee prevail,
To cure the wounds we now bewail;
Oh, bless us with thy holy sight,
And fill us with eternal light.

<h>O</h>ur guide, our way to heavenly rest,
Be thou the aim of every breast;
Be thou the soother of our tears,
Our sweet reward above the spheres.

<h>A</h>ll glory, Lord, to Thee we pay,
Ascending o'er the stars to-day;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Keep us, Lord, as the apple of thine eye, alleluia.
<r>℟.</r> Protect us under the shadow of thy wings, alleluia.

b.3b7f3a5c9a:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>C</c>oncéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui hodiérna die Unigénitum tuum, Redemptórem nostrum, ad cælos ascendísse crédimus; ipsi quoque mente in cæléstibus habitémus.
<h>P</h>er eúndem Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.028980e72c:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that just as we do believe thine Only-Begotten Son, our Saviour, to have this day ascended into the heavens, so we may also in heart and mind thither ascend, and with Him continually dwell.
<h>T</h>hrough the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
